title: AI Brain Explained
description:
Most people think AI memory is one thing. It is actually four distinct types and understanding the difference changes how you build agents entirely.

In-context memory is everything active inside the current chat window. Whatever Claude Code can see right now in this conversation.
External memory is the brain. A folder that lives outside Claude Code entirely. You could delete Claude Code and the brain would still exist. This is what separates a powerful agent from a basic chatbot.

Episodic memory is the record of past interactions. The chat history Claude Code stores over time. This is essentially what ChatGPT was at launch. In-context memory plus episodic memory and nothing else.
Semantic memory is factual structured knowledge that only gets accessed when relevant. An Airtable database full of data sits in semantic memory. If you ask Claude Code to write an email it will never touch that database. If you ask it something that requires that data it will pull it in. On demand, not always on.

Four types. Four jobs. All working together.
